newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard foreshadows budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard foreshadows budget cuts.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday the government would introduce further cuts in the May budget to retrieve savings lost through legislation in the upper house of parliament, the Senate.

"We obviously to the extent that we have lost money in the process of getting legislation through the Senate we'll be wanting to at least retrieve that," Howard told Channel Nine television. "But it won't be another A$7 or A$8 billion."
The total loss of fiscal measures in the Senate was estimated at A$300 million to A$400 million (1997/98 full year-values) out of a total budget tightening of A$7.2 billion.

Treasurer Peter Costello has previously said the Senate's defeat of some individual budget measures meant the government had lost about A$1 billion in fiscal tightening in its second and third years. He said the government planned to use May's budget to recover about A$1 billion lost when the Senate rejected some of the 1996 budget.
The August budget was designed to make budget savings of around A$36 billion over four years.
The Liberal-National government depends on the support of two independent senators to pass legislation through the Senate and has seen some budget bills amended.
